question: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood directly into the systemic circulation?
explanation: The left ventricle has thick muscular walls to forcefully push oxygenated blood through the aortic valve and into the systemic circulation. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why is blood pressure in the systemic circulation much higher than in the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: Deoxygenated blood is thicker than oxygenated blood.
options.B: The lungs require less oxygen than peripheral body tissues.
options.C: The systemic circuit must travel a much greater distance through the entire body.
options.D: The heart beats faster when pumping blood to the lungs.

explanation: Pumping blood through all the organs and limbs of the entire body requires a much higher pressure head than just traveling the short distance to the lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h1)

question: What is the primary role of arterioles in the systemic circulation?

options.A: Regulating local blood distribution and maintaining pressure
options.B: Storing large volumes of reserve blood for emergencies
options.C: Filtering waste products out of circulating red blood cells
options.D: Absorbing dietary fats directly from the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Arterioles have muscular walls that contract or relax to control blood flow into capillary beds and help maintain overall blood pressure. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h2)

question: Identify which structural feature allows main arteries to withstand high pressure without bursting.
explanation: Arteries need thick, elastic walls to stretch and recoil with each heartbeat, handling the high pressure surges straight from the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h2)

question: What structural characteristic of capillaries makes nutrient and gas exchange efficient?

options.A: High concentration of active red blood cells
options.B: Walls that are only a single cell thick
options.C: Direct connections to large distributing veins
options.D: Presence of thick muscular smooth muscle layers

explanation: The extremely thin wall of a capillary allows oxygen, nutrients, and wastes to diffuse across rapidly and easily. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h3)

question: How do oxygen and nutrients primarily move from inside a capillary into surrounding tissue cells?

options.A: Direct injection through tiny valves in the vessel wall
options.B: Passive diffusion down a concentration gradient
options.C: Rapid filtration driven entirely by high venous pressure
options.D: Active transport powered by heavy muscular pumping

explanation: Substances like oxygen move naturally from an area of higher concentration in the blood to an area of lower concentration in the tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h3)

question: Which large blood vessels collect all deoxygenated systemic blood before it enters the right atrium?
explanation: The superior and inferior vena cava are the two major veins that return all deoxygenated blood from the body back to the right atrium of the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the one-way valves found inside medium-sized veins?

options.A: Filtering out harmful bacteria before blood reaches the heart
options.B: Preventing the gravitational backflow of blood in the limbs
options.C: Regulating the exact speed of red blood cell production
options.D: Boosting arterial blood pressure during physical exercise

explanation: Venous valves act like swing doors that only open toward the heart, stopping blood from flowing backward down the legs when a person stands still. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h4)

question: Which factor has the greatest immediate physiological effect on changing systemic vascular resistance?

options.C: Total weight of the skeletal bones
options.D: Total length of the blood vessels

explanation: Even a tiny change in the radius of an arteriole dramatically alters resistance and controls how much blood flows through an organ. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h5)

question: What happens to systemic blood flow if blood vessel resistance increases while pressure remains constant?
explanation: Resistance works against flow; when resistance goes up and pressure stays the same, less fluid can pass through the vessel. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h5)

question: What cardiovascular adaptation commonly occurs in normal healthy pregnancy to support the placenta?

options.A: Permanent narrowing of all major systemic arteries
options.B: Significant increase in total maternal blood volume
options.C: Dramatic drop in resting maternal heart rate
options.D: Complete cessation of activity in the venous valves

explanation: Maternal blood volume expands substantially during pregnancy to ensure adequate perfusion of the growing uterus and placenta. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h6)

question: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks gestation presents with a very high blood pressure reading and severe headache. Which pathological process in the systemic circulation is most likely occurring?

options.A: Sudden widening of capillaries leaking excess water
options.B: Complete failure of the venous valves in her legs
options.C: Massive destruction of red blood cells in the aorta

explanation: Conditions like pre-eclampsia feature abnormal constriction of systemic arterioles, which spikes blood pressure and reduces blood flow to organs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h6)
